newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota recalls more than 160,000 vehicles in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Toyota recalls more than 160,000 vehicles in Japan.

text.p: Japan's top carmaker Toyota Motor Corp on Tuesday announced a big vehicle recall to repair defective brake parts.
Toyota and its affiliates Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd and Hino Motors Ltd said they were recalling nearly 170,000 four-wheel-drive vehicles and light trucks in Japan.
The total repair cost for Toyota is estimated at about three billion yen ($27.5 million) in Japan, a Toyota spokesman said.

Toyota vehicles accounted for 163,761 out of the total number being recalled. The figure comprises 11 Toyota models including the Land Cruiser, Dayna truck, and ToyoAce. Four Daihatsu models totalling 3,192 vehicles, and four Hino models totalling 1,900 vehicles were also being recalled.
They were diesel-engine vehicles made between December 1, 1989, and June 28, 1994, using Nippondenso Co Ltd rotors and blades.
Faulty blades in the brake system could cause a decline in the braking force. No accidents have been reported.
Toyota will also repair the same fault in a total of about 212,000 vehicles exported to 178 countries including Australia, Britain, and Saudi Arabia, the Toyota spokesman said.
Daihatsu will also repair 15,649 vehicles exported to 69 countries. Hino did not export any of the defective vehicles.
Daihatsu's total repair cost is estimated at about 50 million yen ($458,000) in Japan and Hino's total cost is estimated at 32 million yen ($293,000), company spokesmen said.
Toyota owns 23.1 percent of Nippondenso, 33.4 percent of Daihatsu and 11 percent of Hino.

A Japanese Transport Ministry official played down the recall. "This recall is not very big. If the total volume exceeded 300,000 then that would be 20th (in terms of ranking) on our list," he said. ($1=109 yen)
